subject: gov.policy
name: Artificial-intelligence legislation
milestone: Sequenced behind the strategy, per the ICT minister
position_end: Announced as following the strategy; nothing drafted or tabled
note: The research council's own authors recorded no artificial-intelligence governance framework in place at 2026-02-16

subject: gov.policy
name: Cloud computing determination for banking institutions
milestone: BID-19, gazetted 26 November 2024 under the Banking Institutions Act
position_end: The central bank's determination requires banking institutions to ensure that cloud service providers adhere to data protection law including data residency requirements and privacy standards, and to keep the regulator and external auditors reachable; it binds banks rather than government, and is the closest instrument to a hosting rule the base holds
note: Held as an excerpt truncated by the fetch limit

subject: gov.policy
name: National artificial-intelligence strategy
milestone: Consultations reported begun under the research council 2026-08-05
position_end: Under development through the research council's working group and its technical advisory committees, with consultations begun; no draft published, and the ministry states the strategy is sequenced ahead of legislation
note: An earlier report that a consultancy was engaged to lead the framework was resolved against on 2026-08-05

subject: gov.policy
name: National Broadband Policy
milestone: Published by government notice under section 7 of the Communications Act
position_end: Gazetted in August 2020 as the standing broadband instrument; no revision or successor is held

subject: gov.policy
name: National spatial data infrastructure policy
milestone: Published by general notice, March 2015
position_end: Gazetted by the statistics agency as the framework for sharing spatial data across government, and the base's clearest formally adopted cross-government data-sharing instrument; no non-spatial interoperability framework is gazetted

subject: gov.policy
name: Statistics agency data collection, processing and dissemination policy
milestone: Issued February 2014 under the Statistics Act
position_end: The statistics agency's own policy on how it collects, processes and disseminates data, and the base's one operative government data-governance instrument outside the payments and banking sectors

subject: gov.legislate
name: Archives Act, 1992
milestone: Act 12 of 1992, in force from publication
position_end: The Act covers local-authority archives expressly and gives the head of archives authority to inspect and direct local-authority filing and computer and microfilm projects; it is the base's only instrument bearing on how local government keeps records

subject: gov.legislate
name: Corporate Laws Bill 2025
milestone: Draft 3 out for comment by stakeholders and the general public
position_end: At Draft 3 and out for public comment: it consolidates and re-enacts the Companies Act with the business and intellectual property authority as registrar, and clause 114 would require every company, and every external company establishing a place of business in Namibia, to keep in Namibia a register of beneficial owners recording each owner's name, date of birth, identity-document number and residential, business, email and postal addresses; company process is routed through the Electronic Transactions Act
note: The draft carries no date on its face and is dated from the file's own timestamp, so this dates the draft and not a tabling or a gazette

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrime Bill
milestone: Named by the ICT minister as being finalised, 2026-07-14
position_start: No bill named on the record; enforcement relying on the electronic transactions statute, the communications statute and the penal code
position_end: Named by the minister as being finalised alongside the data protection bill; no draft published and no tabling date given
note: The base first names this bill on 2026-07-14

subject: gov.legislate
name: Data Protection Bill
milestone: Tabling promised for September 2025; described as in final polishing in January 2026
position_end: Not tabled and not enacted, and no data-protection statute is in force. The ministry said in August 2025 it would table the Bill that September; in January 2026 the minister described the data protection and cybercrime bills as under final polishing with consultation on the cybercrime bill opening on 2 February
note: The drafting start of about 2013 is inferred from the twelve years reported on 2025-08-17

subject: gov.legislate
name: Data Protection Bill, latest published draft
milestone: Published for comment by the ministry, March 2022
position_start: The March 2022 revised draft, 59 pages and eight Parts, the last version published for comment
position_end: The March 2022 revised draft remains the last version published for comment, with the supervisory authority at its Part 2; the draft's stated objects are establishing a Data Protection Supervisory Authority with its own powers and duties, obligations on data controllers and processors, rights for data subjects, and codes of conduct; the 2020 version is held alongside it, and no later text and no tabling record has been published
note: The March 2022 draft is now held directly rather than known only through the 2020 draft's comparative account

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic signature regulations
milestone: Gazetted 19 December 2025; the enabling provisions commenced June 2026
position_end: Regulations made under the Electronic Transactions Act set the rules for electronic signatures, and the regulator separately gazetted regulations for accrediting security products, services and their providers; the Act's section 20 and its accreditation chapter were brought into force in June 2026

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Transactions Act 2019
milestone: In force from March 2021
position_start: In force; covers electronic signatures, consumer protection and contracts but not cross-border data flow, data localisation or personal data protection
position_end: Unchanged; still the interim instrument law enforcement relies on for cybercrime, with the communications statute and the penal code
sources: 2023-01-01 Digital Trade Regulatory Integration - Namibia Country Profile|2026-07-14-namibia-pushes-cyber-security-reforms-itweb
note: The regulatory profile is a reference study, cited and not absorbed

subject: gov.legislate
name: Payment service provider licensing determination
milestone: PSD-1, effective 6 January 2026
position_end: The central bank's determination brings licensing and authorisation of payment service providers into operation under the 2023 Act, which itself commenced on 8 August 2023

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act, 2011
milestone: Act No. 9 of 2011
position_end: The principal statistics statute, constituting the statistics agency and providing for the national statistics system and the spatial data infrastructure

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-subject rights provisions of the Data Protection Bill
milestone: Part III, sections 8 to 14, present in the 2020 draft and absent from the March 2022 revised draft
position_start: Recorded as removed on a research institute's account; neither draft held
position_end: Established from the drafts themselves: the 2020 version carries Part III, "Rights of the Data Subject", sections 8 to 14, together with Part VII on recourse to the judicial authority and Part VIII on offences and penalties, none of which appears in the 59-page, eight-Part version the ministry published for comment in March 2022, where access and correction survive only as controller obligations at sections 31 and 32
note: The 2020 draft carries no date on its face and is identified by structural match

subject: gov.protect
name: Gazette notice withdrawing existing identity documents
milestone: Provided for; not issued at 2026-08-06
position_end: Named by the home affairs ministry as the instrument that will end the validity of pre-independence cards, older identity documents and current machine-readable cards; not issued
note: Until it issues, the September 2026 rollout is additive

subject: gov.protect
name: Student financial assistance fund data breach
milestone: Breach reported October 2025
position_end: The national incident response team's head called for urgent finalisation of the data protection law after a breach at the students' financial assistance fund; no record count, remedy or sanction is held, because there is no statute under which to impose one

subject: gov.regional
name: Communications regulator and electricity distributor data-sharing memorandum
milestone: Five-year non-binding memorandum signed at Ondangwa, August 2026
position_end: A five-year non-binding memorandum between the communications regulator and the electricity distributor covering information and data sharing and rural electrification; non-binding is the parties’ own description, and no work programme or first exchange is on file

subject: gov.regional
name: Cross-border connectivity memoranda with Botswana
milestone: Government memorandum signed at Kasane, 7 August 2026
position_end: The two ICT ministries signed a framework covering digital transformation, cybersecurity, affordable connectivity and skills development, six months after the two countries' operators signed their own memorandum on cross-border connectivity

subject: gov.regional
name: Namibia's seat on an international artificial-intelligence commission
milestone: The ICT minister named among the commission's members
position_end: The ICT minister is one of eight Africans on a 44-member commission
note: The commission's composition is the convening body's account

subject: gov.regional
name: Namibia-Angola information technology and media memorandum
milestone: Signed at the opening of a technology forum in Luanda
position_end: Covers joint events, exchange of expertise and cybersecurity; no amount or instrument named

subject: gov.regional
name: Namibia-Botswana information and communications technology memorandum
milestone: Signed at Kasane 2026-08-07
position_end: Signed at Kasane on 7 August 2026 between the two ICT ministries with their operators and regulators, covering digital transformation, cybersecurity, connectivity and skills development; the two sides costed the Trans-Kalahari Corridor's remaining 4G gaps at about N$52 million across 13 new sites, recorded the completion of a Gobabis-Buitepos fibre link now interconnecting with the Botswana backbone company at Charles Hill as the first direct cross-border fibre link between the operators, and said their two incident-response teams are deepening cooperation
note: the signed instrument is not held; no term, funding or data-governance provision is published

subject: gov.regional
name: Namibia-Republic of Congo information technology memorandum
milestone: Cabinet approved and authorised signature, announced 2026-07-23
position_end: Approved at cabinet's 22nd and 23rd sittings with the ICT minister authorised to sign; no scope, sector detail, financing or signature date published
note: The text is the thing to acquire

subject: gov.regional
name: Pan-African language artificial-intelligence initiative
milestone: Launched at a continental telecommunications conference with Namibia's ICT ministry a named partner
position_end: Namibia one of five backing governments in a pan-African African-language initiative scaling an existing national model template; no Namibian funding, dataset or deliverable published
note: Namibia's stated commitment is ministerial support, not a named contribution

subject: gov.regional
name: Ratification of the continental convention on cyber security and personal data protection
milestone: Tabled for ratification in Parliament, 2018
position_end: The ICT minister tabled the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection in Parliament for ratification in 2018, and the Union's own status list records the ratification; the domestic statute the Convention calls for is still a Bill

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional regulators' legal and policy committee
milestone: First meeting hosted at Windhoek 10 to 12 August 2026
position_end: Constituted and meeting, with artificial-intelligence governance, data governance and protection, digital public infrastructure and regional regulatory harmonisation on its agenda
note: hosted by the national regulator for the southern African regulators' association; no work programme, output or timetable is published

subject: gov.standards
name: National standardisation strategy
milestone: Launched 15 October 2025, targeting 1,200 new standards in three years
position_end: A strategy launched in October 2025 targets 1,200 new standards over three years, against 235 published since the institution's establishment in 2008 — set beside 1,600 in Botswana, 6,500 in Zambia and more than 10,500 in South Africa; a package covering chilled seafood, marketing quality, laundry and refrigerating appliances was adopted in June 2026

subject: gov.standards
name: Standards Act, 2005
milestone: Act No. 18 of 2005
position_end: The founding statute establishing the national standards institution and its council

subject: gov.discourse
name: Published draft and consultation record of the Data Protection Bill
milestone: Consultation closed 2022-11-30; a coalition submission and an independent critique published
position_end: A dated consultation record: the ministry opened public input on the draft Data Protection Bill on 2022-10-26 with a closing date of 2022-11-30, addressed to two named ministry officers; the ACTION Namibia Coalition filed a submission on the closing date, compiled by ALT Advisory and funded by the Embassy of Finland through IPPR's Democracy Report project; IPPR published the same argument as a public paper on 2022-12-14, arguing the sections on the Supervisory Authority's independence need substantial redrafting and that offences and penalties provisions are undeveloped; no ministry-published list of respondents is held, and no further consultation activity is on record since
note: The IPPR paper and the coalition submission are one argument in two forms, not two independent reviews

subject: gov.discourse
name: Regional consultations on the cybercrime bill
milestone: Consultations opened 4 February 2026
position_end: The ICT ministry took the proposed cybersecurity and cybercrime bill to stakeholders in three northern regions, having said in January that consultations would begin on 2 February; no submission count or consultation report is held

name: United Nations and mobile operator partnership
milestone: Five-year memorandum signed 23 May 2025

name: Corporate-funded regional digital technology hub
milestone: Inaugurated at Ondangwa, 24 June 2026
position_end: A mining-foundation-funded digital technology hub was inaugurated by the President at Ondangwa; the account is of the opening of an upgraded facility and states no capital commitment, so no deal record was built

subject: finance.new
name: Development bank skills and artificial-intelligence programme
milestone: Indicative N$5.62 billion programme
position_end: An indicative N$5.62 billion programme backed by the African Development Bank would modernise vocational institutions, establish a national artificial-intelligence institute and a national data centre, and create 15,000 workplace opportunities; no agreement, disbursement or start date is held

subject: finance.new
name: Private co-investment in the subsea cable landing
milestone: About US$5 million co-landing with a private operator
position_end: The state fixed operator's own account of a roughly US$5 million private co-landing of the subsea cable, the base's clearest record of completed non-state investment in international connectivity

subject: finance.new
name: Private mobile network investment
milestone: The network launched 2025-09-04
position_end: A live network with N$600,000,000 invested in the year to September 2025, company-reported
note: The group figure of N$1.42bn invested since 2018 is context, not this commitment

subject: finance.new
name: Universal Service Fund
milestone: Launched 2025-03-19 with N$145,000,000 of government seed funding over three years
position_start: Operating; N$145,000,000 of seed funding over three years and a N$31,000,000 subsidy already disbursed to the mobile operator for nine network sites (2025-03)
position_end: Operating; priority given to the five regions where 4G coverage is below 80% - Kavango West, Kavango East, Kunene, Ohangwena and Oshikoto - with 16 schools and four clinics selected for uncapped Wi-Fi, and 100 handsets distributed to learners in Kunene in February 2026, and CRAN's own Integrated Annual Report 2025 states the Fund's governance framework was developed and approved by the CRAN Board, with the Ministry's contribution given there as N$115,000,000 over three years and a first bidding round awarding nine sites to MTC with almost N$31,000,000 of capital subsidy across the same five regions, all schools and health facilities on those sites to receive free internet for seven years

subject: finance.new
name: Universal service fund phase 2 agreement
milestone: Signed 9 April 2026; N$9,796,650 subsidy
position_end: The state fixed operator won a subsidy of N$9,796,650 through a bidding process, to deploy telecommunications infrastructure at sites in underserved rural areas; no site list, completion date or coverage target is held

subject: finance.new
name: Universal service levy
milestone: Regulations Prescribing Universal Service Levy made 2024-09-27 (Government Gazette 8455, General Notice 559), effective on publication
position_start: A 2022 notice of intention (Government Gazette 7860, General Notice 342, 25 July 2022) withdrawn 2024-06-21 (Government Gazette 8384, General Notice 291) pending a revised evidence base
position_end: In force from 2024-09-27: levy not exceeding 0.5% of annual turnover per licensee (regulation 4 and Annexure A), a flat N$500 floor for non-profit licensees, invoiced on audited or sworn financial statements and payable within 30 days into the Universal Service Fund; regulation 9 and Annexure B amended the 2018 universal service regulations to let the Fund receive donations or grants, which is what makes the Government of Namibia's committed funding receivable; CRAN's own reply to comments states the Gap Analysis identifies 119 locations that will remain unserved after 700/800 MHz roll-out obligations, of which government funding covers the capital cost of 42
note: The notice of intention that preceded withdrawal set the levy at 5% in its operative regulation text against 1% in the assessment formula everyone including the regulator actually consulted on; the final regulations resolve both to 0.5%, a halving of the formula rate

subject: finance.new
name: World Bank country partnership framework
milestone: Covers FY25 to FY29
position_end: The governing framework for the period sets up to US$400 million of lending from the bank and up to US$200 million of potential corporation financing; no digital allocation inside it is stated

subject: infra.connect

milestone: Applied to refuse a licence 2026-03-23, the refusal upheld 2026-06-22
position_start: In force, with a foreign-ownership exemption bid under ministerial review
position_end: In force; no exemption granted, and the regulator held that wholly foreign ownership raises questions of jurisdiction, enforceability of compliance obligations and effective oversight

subject: infra.connect
name: Backbone modernisation and route redundancy
milestone: New long-distance routes laid; second open-access partnership signed 8 June 2026
position_end: The state fixed operator says it is laying new long-distance fibre routes and creating redundant paths between key cities and regions after network failures, and signed a second open-access fibre partnership in June 2026, live in five named localities

subject: infra.connect
name: Commercial 5G network
milestone: Commercial launch at end-August 2025 in three centres
position_end: Live in Windhoek, Swakopmund and Walvis Bay; nationwide deployment stated as intended, phased and city-first
sources: 2025-09-23-namibia-expedites-data-centre-smart-city-development-itweb|2026-02-10-towards-5g-enabled-digitalized-namibia-2026-telecomreviewafrica|2025-06-04 Namibia targets 100% telecom coverage nationwide by 2030

subject: infra.connect
name: CRAN Integrated Annual Report
milestone: Integrated Annual Report 2025 approved by the Board 2025-08-07, covering the year to 31 March 2025
position_start: Integrated Annual Report 2024 (approved 2024-09-06, year to 31 March 2024): a funding proposal secured a N$115 million, three-year Universal Service Fund commitment from the Government of Namibia; broadband coverage of schools rose 31.5 points to 81.5% and of clinics 38.9 points to 88.9%; total assets N$277.9 million, up N$29.6 million
position_end: Integrated Annual Report 2025 (approved 2025-08-07, year to 31 March 2025): the Universal Service Fund's governance framework was approved and the Fund launched 2025-03-19 with the N$115 million MICT commitment; a first bidding round awarded nine sites to MTC with almost N$31 million capital subsidy across Kunene, Kavango East, Kavango West, Ohangwena and Oshikoto, with free internet for schools and clinics on the new sites for seven years; revenue fell 23% to 15.5% below budget, operating expenditure rose 42% to N$143.1 million, and a N$32.8 million surplus became a N$25.5 million loss; 4G population coverage 91% and an ITU ICT Development Index of 73.2% are separately stated
note: The Fund's own launch account here (N$115m over three years) differs from the press-reported N$145m seed-funding figure the wiki holds on the Universal Service Fund row for the same 2025-03-19 launch; the two are not reconciled

subject: infra.connect
name: Determination of dominant position in the telecommunications market
milestone: 2024 determination gazetted 2024-08-15 (Government Gazette 8416, General Notice 456); the four market definitions unchanged from 2016
position_start: 2016 determination (Government Gazette 6054, General Notice 214, 28 June 2016) defined the four priority markets carried forward in 2024: fixed and mobile call/SMS termination, wired end-user access, national data transmission, and wireless end-user access
position_end: 2024 determination names Telecom Namibia dominant in all four markets - alone in wired end-user access, with NamPower in national data transmission, with MTC in wireless end-user access, and with MTC, UCom Mobile, Paratus and Telepassport in call and SMS termination, termination being treated as a natural monopoly; CRAN describes its approach across all three exercises (2013, 2016, 2024) as one of minimal intervention
note: The 2012/13 determination (Government Gazette 5201, General Notice 167, 29 May 2013) covered telecommunications and broadcasting only and named Mobile Telecommunications Limited, Powercom (Leo) and Telecom Namibia; neither the 2012/13 nor 2016 determination text is separately held, only CRAN's own account of them in the 2024 gazette

subject: infra.connect
name: First privately owned mobile network
milestone: Launched 2025-09-02
position_end: A national network live on long-term evolution and 5G; N$600m invested in the network in the preceding year and N$1.42bn in Namibian network infrastructure since 2018, company-reported
note: The pre-launch account describes a data-only network and the launch account data and voice

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet penetration

subject: infra.connect
name: Ministry strategic plan 2025-2030 and national ICT policy
milestone: Launched at Opuwo 2026-01-29
position_end: In force; priorities are affordable broadband and mobile coverage in rural and underserved areas, cybersecurity, data protection and electronic government; the policy names high data costs, limited infrastructure and unequal access as the barriers

position_end: N$624.9 million committed to telecommunications infrastructure in the 2025/26 financial year
note: The operator’s own stated commitment, not a delivered figure.

subject: infra.connect

position_end: Signed by the state fixed operator with two Angolan counterparts, with the Namibian operator as landing party hosting Angolan equipment; scope covers design, integration, testing, commissioning and handover

subject: infra.connect
name: Regulator coverage and subscriber statistics
milestone: Latest published series reports 2023 data
position_end: Published inside the sector market reports: 4G population coverage 85% in 2022, with six of Namibia's 14 regions below 80% and Kunene lowest at 41%; 456 of 1,380 schools and 84 of 452 health facilities without 4G coverage in 2022; about 2,000,000 of 2,900,000 mobile SIM cards actively used for internet access in 2022; and state influence over 87% of telecommunication assets and 83% of sector revenue in 2022, moving to 82% and 80% in 2023; the 2023 edition separately gives 4G population coverage of 88.4%, FTTH at 27% of fixed broadband subscribers (more than double its 2018 share), a 6% fall in active SIM cards, and a rise from 46th to 8th in African 1GB-affordability ranking between Q1 2022 and Q1 2023, which CRAN attributes to its own broadband-price consultation

subject: infra.connect

milestone: Operators instructed to retire the networks and refarm the spectrum
position_end: The regulator has instructed operators to retire 2G and 3G and refarm the spectrum for 4G and 5G; the incumbent asked government at a parliamentary committee hearing on 17 August 2026 to subsidise smartphones before the switch-off, and reported 53 sites in one Kavango region against 39 in the other, of which 50 carry 4G and one 5G
note: no switch-off date and no government response on subsidies is on file

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink operating licence

position_start: An ownership-exemption bid under ministerial review; no licence; a November 2024 cease-and-desist in force

subject: infra.connect
name: Subsea cable station at Swakopmund
milestone: Inaugurated 31 July 2024 with a 100G link activated
